title: RDS: PostgreSQL, MySQL, MariaDB, Oracle and SQL Server

videos.script: Quitanda's orders live in PostgreSQL, on one server in a cupboard of the office. Somebody patches it when they remember, and a cron job copies it to a disk next to it every night. {{cupboard}} RDS is AWS's offer to take that server away. The hardware, the operating system, the backups and the failover become AWS's job. {{managed}} What stays yours is everything inside the database. The schema, the slow query, the missing index, the number of connections. And the bill. {{yours}} You will create the instance in moto, with its network, its password kept out of your terminal and its own configuration. It becomes available on the very same line. {{create}} Nothing is behind it. There is a name, a status and an address, and no database engine at all. That difference is the most useful thing moto teaches about RDS. {{nothing}} Then you change two settings, and find out why one of them needs a restart. {{params}} And you price four instances for a month, with the licence included and without it. One of them costs almost five times another on the same size of machine. {{price}}
